lessons.0.slides.0.title: Why Vintage Matters
lessons.0.slides.0.subtitle: 15 minutes
lessons.0.slides.0.description: Burgundy lies on the northern edge of viable viticulture and the climate swings widely from year to year. Understanding vintage is the key to appreciating Burgundy.
lessons.0.slides.1.title: Why Is Vintage So Important in Burgundy?
lessons.0.slides.1.content: Burgundy sits at the northern frontier of viticulture (latitude 47° N), where climate swings widely and every vintage has its own personality.
lessons.0.slides.1.keyPoints.1: • 47° N — the northern edge of viticulture
lessons.0.slides.1.keyPoints.6: • Spring frost shapes the crop size
lessons.0.slides.1.keyPoints.17: 💡 Same estate, same vineyard — different vintages, very different wines
lessons.0.slides.2.title: Four Climate Factors That Shape a Vintage
lessons.0.slides.2.content: Temperature, rainfall, sunlight and frost are the four levers that determine vintage quality.
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.2: • Too hot: high alcohol, lack of finesse
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.3: • Too cold: high acidity, lean fruit
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.4: • Ideal: a warm but not hot summer
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.7: • Too much: dilutes flavour, raises disease risk
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.8: • Too little: vine stress, low yields
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.9: • Ideal: enough during growth, dry at harvest
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.12: • Determines skin thickness and tannin quality
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.13: • Drives colour depth and aromatic intensity
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.19: • Surviving grapes often show better quality
lessons.0.slides.3.title: ⭐ 2015 — The Vintage of the Century
lessons.0.slides.3.content: Widely regarded as a vintage of the century, with reds and whites both excelling and remarkable ageing potential.
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.10: • Already sitting at the top of the market
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.11: • A first choice for investment and collection
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.14: • Reds: entering their drinking window from 2025
lessons.0.slides.4.title: ⭐ 2018 & 2020 — The Twin Stars
lessons.0.slides.4.content: Two outstanding vintages with distinctive characters — both very much worth collecting.
lessons.0.slides.4.keyPoints.6: • Best for: lovers of opulent styles
lessons.0.slides.4.keyPoints.14: • Best for: those seeking classic Burgundy style
lessons.0.slides.4.keyPoints.16: 💡 2018 leans New World; 2020 is more classic
lessons.0.slides.5.title: ⭐ 2019 & 2022 — Easy-Drinking Vintages
lessons.0.slides.5.content: Excellent vintages with abundant fruit, great drinkability and friendlier prices.
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.2: • Style: fruit-rich, supple and easy to drink
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.6: • Best for: drinking now, entry-level collecting
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.10: • Style: hot and dry, highly concentrated
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.12: • Reds: rich but possibly lacking freshness
lessons.0.slides.5.keyPoints.16: 💡 2019 is great now; 2022 whites are worth cellaring
lessons.0.slides.6.title: ❄️ 2021 & 2017 — Frost Vintages
lessons.0.slides.6.content: Spring frosts cut yields, but the surviving fruit was of good quality, often with attractive value.
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.5: • Price: high because of low yields
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.10: • Yields: down 40–50% (one of the worst on record)
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.11: • Style: solid quality but very small quantities
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.12: • Character: surviving grapes were of excellent quality
lessons.0.slides.6.keyPoints.16: 💡 Frost vintages produce little wine but the quality isn't bad — value depends on price
lessons.0.slides.7.title: How to Choose a Vintage
lessons.0.slides.7.content: Pick the right vintage for your needs and budget.
lessons.0.slides.7.keyPoints.7: → Character: solid structure, great ageing potential
lessons.0.slides.7.keyPoints.15: → Vintages of the century, strong upside
lessons.0.slides.8.title: 📊 Burgundy Vintage Timeline (2015–2022)
lessons.0.slides.8.content: An overview of recent vintage quality and character, based on consensus among international critics.
lessons.0.slides.8.data.items.0.label: Vintage of the century — outstanding for both reds and whites
lessons.0.slides.8.data.items.1.label: Frost-reduced yields — good quality
lessons.0.slides.8.data.items.2.label: April frost — a scarce vintage
lessons.0.slides.8.data.items.3.label: Hot vintage — rich and full
lessons.0.slides.8.data.items.4.label: Fruit bomb — supple and easy
lessons.0.slides.8.data.items.5.label: Model of balance — classic style
lessons.0.slides.8.data.items.6.label: Severe frost — reds outperform whites
lessons.0.slides.8.data.items.7.label: A white-wine year — hot and dry
lessons.0.slides.8.note: Scores are guidance only — personal taste and budget matter more. Vintages of the century suit collecting; ordinary vintages offer better value.
lessons.0.slides.9.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.0.slides.9.points.0: 🍷 Burgundy lies at the northern edge — vintage variation is huge
lessons.0.slides.9.points.1: 🍷 2015, 2020 and 2018 are the three outstanding recent vintages
lessons.0.slides.9.points.2: 🍷 2019 and 2022 are fruit-rich and very drinkable
lessons.0.slides.9.points.3: 🍷 Frost vintages (2017, 2021) deliver less wine but solid quality
lessons.0.slides.9.points.4: 🍷 For drinking now go for 2019; for cellaring go for 2020/2015
lessons.0.slides.9.points.5: 🍷 Whites: 2022 is the top pick; reds: 2020 is the top pick
lessons.0.slides.10.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.0.question: Why is vintage particularly important in Burgundy?
A. Burgundy changes its grape varieties every year
B. The continental climate varies sharply year to year — quality differences between good and poor vintages are vast
C. The vintage is purely decorative on the label
D. Burgundy regulations change every three years
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.0.explanat: Burgundy's continental climate swings dramatically from year to year — a single hailstorm, early frost or rainy spell can ruin an entire vintage. Choosing the right vintage is therefore critical to assessing Burgundy quality, far more so than in maritime regions like Bordeaux.
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.1.question: Among Burgundy's recent widely-acclaimed "great vintages", which 2010s year is most often cited?
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.1.explanat: 2015 is widely regarded as the top Burgundy vintage of the past decade — warm climate, healthy harvest, and outstanding both for reds and whites. 2019 and 2020 are also excellent. Each vintage has its own profile, and a vintage guide is essential for accurate evaluation.
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.2.question: Which of the following are Burgundy's most legendary top domaines? (multiple answers)
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.2.explanat: DRC (Romanée-Conti), Armand Rousseau (the Gevrey legend of the Côte de Nuits) and Leroy (famed for ultra-low yields and ultra-high quality) are all top Burgundy domaines. Mouton Rothschild is a Médoc Bordeaux estate, not a Burgundy producer.
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.3.question: Which of the following is one of Burgundy's most famous Négociant-Éleveurs?
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.3.explanat: Louis Jadot is Burgundy's best-known négociant-éleveur, buying grapes or wines from many growers, then ageing, bottling and selling them under its own label. It exports to markets worldwide and is one of the most globally recognised Burgundy brands.
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.4.question: Which winemaking practices are seen as guarantees of Domaine Leroy's top quality? (multiple answers)
B. Extremely low yields (only a few clusters left on each vine)
C. Heavy use of mechanical harvesting to cut costs
lessons.0.slides.10.questions.4.explanat: Domaine Leroy is famed for rigorous biodynamic farming and tiny yields: production is far below legal limits, and only a few clusters per vine are kept to maximise concentration. The fruit is hand-harvested, aged in a high proportion of new oak, producing rich wines that age for decades.
lessons.0.slides.11.title: Summary
lessons.0.slides.11.content: Vintage is the key to appreciating Burgundy. Understand the impact of climate on the wine and you can choose what suits you best. Vintages of the century are worth collecting; ordinary vintages offer better value. Remember: there is no perfect vintage, only the vintage that's right for you.

lessons.1.slides.2.content: The king of Burgundy — the world's most exalted estate, owner of several legendary Grand Crus.
lessons.1.slides.2.keyPoints.1: 👑 Status: King of Burgundy — the undisputed No. 1
lessons.1.slides.2.keyPoints.16: 💰 Price: €€€€€ (tens to hundreds of thousands of NTD)
lessons.1.slides.2.keyPoints.17: 🏆 Romanée-Conti is the most expensive wine in the world
lessons.1.slides.3.title: 🌟 Domaine Leroy
lessons.1.slides.3.content: A pioneer of biodynamic viticulture, sitting at the very top alongside DRC.
lessons.1.slides.3.keyPoints.1: 👤 Owner: the late Lalou Bize-Leroy (former co-owner of DRC)
lessons.1.slides.4.title: 🏆 Domaine Armand Rousseau
lessons.1.slides.4.content: The leading producer of Gevrey-Chambertin — a perfect marriage of elegance and power.
lessons.1.slides.4.keyPoints.7: • Clos Saint-Jacques (a Premier Cru, but Grand Cru in quality)
lessons.1.slides.4.keyPoints.10: • Elegance and power in perfect balance
lessons.1.slides.4.keyPoints.15: 💰 Price: €€€€ (thousands to tens of thousands of NTD)
lessons.1.slides.5.title: 🥂 Domaine Leflaive
lessons.1.slides.5.content: King of Puligny-Montrachet whites — the model of refined, mineral Chardonnay.
lessons.1.slides.5.keyPoints.1: 🏆 Status: a top white-wine domaine of Burgundy
lessons.1.slides.5.keyPoints.19: 💰 Price: €€€€ (thousands to tens of thousands of NTD)
lessons.1.slides.6.title: 🍯 Domaine Coche-Dury
lessons.1.slides.6.content: The Meursault legend — rich, complex, oxidative-style whites.
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.15: 🔥 Demand: bottles are nearly impossible to find
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.17: 💡 Production is tiny; most goes to long-standing customers
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.18: 🏆 The ultimate expression of the Meursault style
lessons.1.slides.7.title: ❄️ Domaine Raveneau
lessons.1.slides.7.content: The benchmark of Chablis Grand Cru — the standard-bearer of pure, mineral whites.
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.6: • Montée de Tonnerre (a Premier Cru, but Grand Cru in quality)
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.18: 💰 Price: €€€€ (thousands to tens of thousands of NTD)
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.19: 🏆 The benchmark of Chablis — a top collecting choice
lessons.1.slides.8.title: 🌱 Rising Quality Estates
lessons.1.slides.8.content: A new generation of estates upholding tradition while daring to innovate.
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.2: • Owner of Clos des Lambrays (Grand Cru, almost a monopole)
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.18: • Chambertin and Latricières Grand Cru holdings

lessons.1.slides.9.content: Pick the right estate and cuvée for your budget and needs.

lessons.1.slides.10.points.0: 🍷 DRC is the king of Burgundy — the undisputed No. 1

lessons.2.slides.0.description: Learn how to build a personal cellar, store wine well and develop your tasting skills, ready to enjoy Burgundy for the long run.
lessons.2.slides.1.title: Why Collect Burgundy?
lessons.2.slides.1.content: Burgundy is more than great wine — it's an art of time and a target for investment.
lessons.2.slides.1.keyPoints.7: • Vintages of the century have strong upside
lessons.2.slides.1.keyPoints.8: • Rare cuvées are even more collectible
lessons.2.slides.1.keyPoints.19: 💡 Collecting is a long-term commitment and pleasure
lessons.2.slides.2.title: 💰 Entry-Level Collecting (€500–1,000 budget)
lessons.2.slides.2.content: Build a foundational cellar and explore different villages and styles.
lessons.2.slides.2.keyPoints.1: • Choose quality village-level and Premier Cru wines
lessons.2.slides.2.keyPoints.16: • Buy 2–3 bottles per village (for comparative tasting)
lessons.2.slides.2.keyPoints.18: • Start exploring with the Côte de Nuits
lessons.2.slides.3.title: 💰 Intermediate Collecting (€2,000–5,000 budget)
lessons.2.slides.3.content: Collect Grand Crus and top Premiers Crus to deepen your tasting.
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.1: • Target Grands Crus and top Premiers Crus
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.3: • Start paying attention to top estates
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.17: • Start collecting wines that will age 10–20 years
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.18: • Try entry-level cuvées from the very top estates
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.19: • Attend tastings to build your network
lessons.2.slides.4.title: 💰 Investment Collecting (€10,000+ budget)
lessons.2.slides.4.content: Collect the very top estates and vintages of the century — a balance of pleasure and investment.
lessons.2.slides.4.keyPoints.1: • Target top estates like DRC and Leroy
lessons.2.slides.5.title: 🏠 Storage Conditions: The Four Essentials
lessons.2.slides.5.content: Proper storage is the key to successful ageing.
lessons.2.slides.5.keyPoints.4: • Variations of more than 5°C harm the wine
lessons.2.slides.5.keyPoints.8: • Too low: corks dry out, wine oxidises
lessons.2.slides.5.keyPoints.9: • Too high: labels mould, corks rot
lessons.2.slides.5.keyPoints.13: • Use a blackout cover or a cellar
lessons.2.slides.5.keyPoints.17: • Lay flat: keeps the cork moist
lessons.2.slides.6.title: ⏳ A Drinking-Window Guide
lessons.2.slides.6.content: Different tiers have different drinking windows — picking the right moment matters.
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.4: • Character: fruit-driven, not for long ageing
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.18: 💡 Whites usually enter their drinking window 5 years earlier than reds
lessons.2.slides.6.keyPoints.19: 💡 Top vintages can extend the drinking window by 5–10 years
lessons.2.slides.7.title: 🍷 Advanced Tasting (1): Vertical Tasting
lessons.2.slides.7.content: Compare different vintages of the same wine to grasp vintage variation and age-related change.
lessons.2.slides.7.keyPoints.6: • Pick the same estate and same vineyard
lessons.2.slides.7.keyPoints.9: • Note the character of each vintage
lessons.2.slides.7.keyPoints.17: • Getting to know a specific estate or vineyard in depth
lessons.2.slides.8.title: 🍷 Advanced Tasting (2): Horizontal Tasting
lessons.2.slides.8.content: Compare the same vintage across different estates or vineyards to grasp differences in terroir and winemaking.
lessons.2.slides.8.keyPoints.1: • Compare the terroirs of different vineyards
lessons.2.slides.8.keyPoints.2: • Compare the styles of different estates
lessons.2.slides.8.keyPoints.7: • Line up 3–6 different estates or vineyards
lessons.2.slides.8.keyPoints.8: • Order by location or by estate
lessons.2.slides.8.keyPoints.14: • Across regions: Meursault vs Puligny vs Chassagne, 2020
lessons.2.slides.8.keyPoints.18: • Choosing your favourite estate or style
lessons.2.slides.9.title: 🍷 Advanced Tasting (3): Blind Tasting
lessons.2.slides.9.content: Tasting without seeing the label sharpens your senses and your focus.
lessons.2.slides.9.keyPoints.6: • Have a friend prepare the wines (covering the labels)
lessons.2.slides.9.keyPoints.8: • Try to identify region, village and vintage
lessons.2.slides.9.keyPoints.9: • Reveal the answers at the end
lessons.2.slides.10.title: 📝 Tasting Notes: Building a Personal Database
lessons.2.slides.10.content: Systematically log your tasting experiences and accumulate personal knowledge.
lessons.2.slides.11.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.2.slides.11.points.0: 🍷 Collecting is a long-term commitment and pleasure
lessons.2.slides.11.points.1: 🍷 Start with village-level and Premier Cru wines
lessons.2.slides.11.points.2: 🍷 Move on to Grands Crus and top estates as you go further
lessons.2.slides.11.points.3: 🍷 For investment, target vintages of the century
lessons.2.slides.11.points.5: 🍷 Vertical tastings reveal vintage; horizontal tastings reveal terroir
lessons.2.slides.11.points.6: 🍷 Keep notes and build your personal database

lessons.2.slides.13.title: Summary
lessons.2.slides.13.content: Collecting Burgundy is a long journey that rewards patience, knowledge and passion. From entry-level collecting to investment, every stage brings its own pleasures and challenges. Proper storage, thoughtful tasting and systematic note-taking are the keys to success. Remember: the point of collecting is to enjoy, not to show off.
